text:
Anna (PM): Quick sync — drafting the launch acceptance gates for Private deployments where customers manage networking. I want a concise, customer-facing checklist we can hand to field + sales. What are the minimal operational guarantees we can commit to?

Raj (Eng): +1. My view: 1) Installer provides a non-destructive upgrade path (rolling, agent-based) 2) IP/ASN preservation option documented 3) Preflight checks that fail fast with clear remediation steps 4) Fallback routing to hosted control plane for telemetry

Marta (Field): Customers keep asking about 'no IP churn' and support during cutovers. We need explicit SLA language for migration windows and a supported rollback path. Also: will we provide an operator-run option vs. self-service?

Kyle (NetOps): From netops side: we need to verify egress IP stability, BGP handoff checklist, and how we surface NAT/external IPs in the installer output. If we promise IP preservation we need a verified mapping and test harness.

Jia (SRE): Don’t forget observability: we must ship a minimal metrics set for upgrade health + an event log that correlates to operator actions. Telemetry must be controllable (on/off) and honor customer KMS settings.

Raj (Eng): Proposed acceptance gates (short):
- Preflight: network, disk, kernel version, iptables, required ports open, control-plane reachability (if opted)
- Upgrade behavior: can do canary 10% tenants -> 100% without operator intervention or with explicit operator gate
- Rollback: documented rollback steps that restore previous agent and ip state in <30 mins for supported configs
- Packaging: airgap tarball + online installer + sha256-signed artifacts
- Security: KMS-integrated secret rotation, audit log export

Anna (PM): Love that. Can we make those into a one-page checklist for field? Short bullets only. Also call out what we cannot guarantee (e.g., customer-managed BGP misconfig).

Marta (Field): Agreed. One-pager needs explicit "customer responsibilities" column: BGP prep, IP allocations, firewall rule changes, DNS cutover windows. Otherwise we get blindsided.

Raj (Eng): Draft one-pager snippet below (feel free to copy):

```
PRIVATE DEPLOY LAUNCH GATES (minimum)
- Preflight OK: network, ports, disk, kernel, ip mappings
- Upgrade path verified: rolling agents, canary policy, rollback trained
- IP stability: documented plan + test plan signed by customer network owner
- Packaging: online installer + airgapped bundle with checksums
- Observability: health metrics + event log enabled, opt-out via KMS policy
- Support SLA: 4h P1 triage, 24h field assistance for complex cutovers (contracted)
- Exclusions: misconfigured customer BGP, in-rack hardware failures, unsupported kernel mods
```

Kyle (NetOps): Add: "Test harness: run a dry-run that simulates BGP handoff and verifies egress IP continuity" – this is a gating step for us to accept the cutover.

Jia (SRE): For telemetry privacy, we should include explicit steps for customers to opt into sanitization. Also need a short troubleshooting playbook for common failure modes.

Anna (PM): Good. Next: Who will own the one-pager and create the field-facing checklist? I can draft the copy but need engineering + netops signoff before EOW.

Raj (Eng): I'll own the preflight checklist items and the upgrade/rollback details. ETA: Tue EOD.

Kyle (NetOps): I'll provide the BGP test procedure and the egress ip verification checklist. ETA: Tue EOD as well.

Marta (Field): I'll draft the customer responsibilities column and a short FAQ from prior deals. ETA: Wed morning.

Jia (SRE): I'll assemble the telemetry + troubleshooting playbook and provide the minimal metrics set. ETA: Wed noon.

Anna (PM): Great. Once all pieces in, I'll synthesize into the one-pager and an internal checklist for sales handoff. Final question: do we want a hard launch gate that blocks GA until we have 2 customer-verified cutovers on v1? Thoughts?

Marta (Field): Strong yes. We should require at least two successful field cutovers on distinct network topologies (on-prem BGP + cloud VPC) before GA messaging.

Raj (Eng): I'm OK with that. We should define "successful" as: upgrade + rollback exercised during scheduled window, metrics cleaned up, no IP drift.

Kyle (NetOps): Agreed. Add that one of the cutovers should include an airgapped/airgap-like flow. 

Anna (PM): Perfect — will add to the launch criteria doc. I'll ping when draft is ready for signoff. Thanks everyone. :pray:

deploy-bot: New doc uploaded: /docs/private-deploy/launch-gates-v1.md (internal)

Marta (Field): noted, will review once Anna shares the draft. :eyes:
